title: Identity and composition normalization of ringed projection mates
statement:
Identity and composition normalization of ringed projection mates. In the existing RingedTensorCorner, RingedTensorModel and RingedTensorEdge interfaces, with TensorConstraints and the normalized comparison predicates of lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition, assert exactly the following independent part of its coherence calculation:

theorem ringedProjectionCanonicalNormalization
    {X Y Z : RingedTensorCorner.{u, w}}
    (f : RingedTensorEdge Y X) (g : RingedTensorEdge Z Y)
    (a : RingedTensorModel X) (b : RingedTensorModel Y) (c : RingedTensorModel Z) :
    (∀ (h : RingedTensorEdge X X) (s : Identity h),
        ∃ l : h.left ≅ 𝟭 X.mateDerived, s.Normalized l ∧
          ∀ (E Q : X.mateDerived),
            h.projection a a E Q ≫
                (identityRight h l).hom.app (X.tensor.obj (E, h.left.obj Q)) ≫
                X.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 E) (l.hom.app Q)) =
              X.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom ((identityRight h l).hom.app E) (𝟙 Q))) ∧
    (∀ (h : RingedTensorEdge Z X) (s : Composition f g h),
        ∃ l : h.left ≅ g.left ⋙ f.left, s.Normalized l ∧
          (∀ (E : X.mateDerived) (Q : Z.mateDerived),
            h.projection c a E Q ≫
                (compositionRight f g h l).hom.app (X.tensor.obj (E, h.left.obj Q)) ≫
                g.right.map (f.right.map
                  (X.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 E) (l.hom.app Q)))) =
              Z.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom ((compositionRight f g h l).hom.app E) (𝟙 Q)) ≫
                g.projection c b (f.right.obj E) Q ≫
                g.right.map (f.projection b a E (g.left.obj Q))))

proof.text: Use the structural identity and composition comparisons, including their normalization and tensor equations. For an isomorphism l between left adjoints, transpose the projection square through the target adjunction. Conjugate-counit compatibility and l naturality move the projection transpose to the other side. The tensor compatibility of l identifies the tensor comparisons; counit compatibility cancels the remaining first-factor map. Apply this calculation to identityTensor and compositeTensor. The identity Hom equivalence is identity; for composition the composite counit and tensorator naturality give the two successive projections. Apply the same conjugate calculation to the structural section comparison to prove sectionProjectionComparison.
